sentences.text: 1. The appellants are the original claimants before this Court.

Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 9.5.2017 passed by the MACP (Aux), NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 undefined Panchmahals at Godhra in MACP no.1835 of 2008, the appellants have preferred this appeal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for sake of brevity).
2.
The claimants are the legal heirs and representatives of the deceased - Baluben Chimanbhai Thakor who died in a vehicular accident, which took place on 2.11.2008.
3. It is the case of the appellants that the deceased was traveling along with appellants no.1 and 3 in Chhakado rickshaw no.GJ-17 U- 5575 driven by opponent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.
The opponent no.1 lost control over the vehicle and collided with the motorcycle and pedestrians and thereby, the rickshaw got turned turtle leading to death of the deceased.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 undefined 4.
It is submitted by Mr. Hemal Shah, learned advocate for the appellants that the appellants were before the Tribunal as the heirs of the deceased who was mother of both the appellants.

It is submitted that the appellant no.2 was eye-witness to the accident, while opponent no.1 had not been examined and thus, submits that the opponent no.1 had been solely held negligent for the occurrence.
Mr. Shah submits that no challenge has been given to the said findings of the Tribunal.

5. Mr. Shah further submits that the claimants are aggrieved as the learned Tribunal has not assessed the income of the deceased who was running a Mahila Gruh Udhyog and was earning Rs.8,000/- to Rs.10,000/- per month.

6. While countering the said argument, Mr. Hardik Mehta, learned advocate for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 undefined opponent no.2 submits that the said deposition was given by the claimants without any documentary evidence to substantiate the fact that the deceased was running a Mahila Gruh Udhyog and thus, stated that at the most, the deceased could be considered as a housewife or at the most can be assessed equivalent to a labourer under minimum wages schedule.

7. Mr. Shah further submits that the learned Tribunal has failed to consider that the husband of the deceased - father of both the claimants had died during pendency of the claim petition and both the claimants are entitled for consortium money as they lost the mother and stated that the amount under the head of loss of estate and funeral charges are not in accordance to the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court; while NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED:
Chimanbhai Kalyansinh Thakor ... vs Prabhat Chhaganbhai Patel on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146076292/
2 17/01/2023 undefined Mr. Mehta submits that sufficient amount of R.40,000/- has been awarded for love and affection.
8.

sentences.text:
The learned Tribunal has granted the compensation under following heads:-
Rs.3,24,800/- Future loss of dependency Rs.10,000/- Funeral & other expenses Rs.40,000/- Love and affection Rs.3,74,800/- Total compensation 9.

In view of the fact that the claimants could not produce any documentary evidence to substantiate that the deceased was having a Gruh Udyog at her house, she could be under the category of being a housewife and further, if the date of accident is taken into consideration and the deceased could be considered as skilled labourer, then, as per the minimum wage schedule declared in the State of Gujarat, an amount of Rs.3,000/- per month could be considered for a skilled NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 undefined person.
Hence, monthly income of the deceased is considered at Rs.3,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has considered the age of the deceased as 45.

Thus, keeping in mind the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, the claimants would be entitled to multiplier of 14 for the compensation and further by following the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, since the deceased was between the age group of 40-45 years, 25% future prospective rise is to be considered.

Hence, the calculation would be as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2420/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 undefined Rs.3,000/- Income per month + Rs.750/- 25% prospective rise in income = Rs.3,750/- Income per month - Rs.1,250/- one-third deduction = Rs.2,500/- Income per month 10.

Considering the monthly income of Rs.2,500/-
and applying multiplier of 14, with the annual income under the head of future loss of dependency,
amount would come to Rs.4,20,000/- (Rs.2,500/- X 14 X 12).

Each claimant as a son would be entitled for consortium amount as per the judgment in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors., (2018) 18 SCC 130 at Rs.40,000/- each.

As the Tribunal has granted Rs.3,74,800/-, the appellants-claimants would be entitled to additional amount of Rs.1,55,200/-.
The learned Tribunal has granted 9% interest per annum.
However, while taking into consideration the current rate of interest, the additional amount be deposited by the insurance Company at the rate of 7.5% interest per annum.
The insurance Company is directed to deposit Rs.1,55,200/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum within eight weeks from the date of receipt of writ of this Court.
